newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb to new record close on GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb to new record close on GDP.

text.p: Profit-takers ate into an earlier intraday high, but Mexican stocks still managed to notch up their fourth record close in six sessions after strong GDP data sent local and foreign bulls into the market, traders said.

"There's a virtuous circle in the economy which offers a bright outlook for this year, which the bourse translated into a rally," Rodolfo Campuzano, an equity analyst at the Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
Final figures showed the leading IPC share index .MXX was up 32.34 points, or 0.84 percent, at 3,875.04.
Volume .TV.MX was heavy at 115.01 million shares traded and reflected greater participation by foreign brokers, traders said.
Mexico's Finance Ministry announced shortly before the opening bell rang that 1996 gross domestic product was up 5.1 percent from 1995, and fourth quarter GDP was up 7.6 percent from a year earlier.
A prior Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms MXAAP showed an average forecast of 4.65 percent for the year and 5.25 percent for the final quarter.
Dealers drew attention to an ebullient mood on the trading floor, where they shouted and elbowed their way to settle an unusually high number of 6,109 trades.
"Dealing was heavy, it was a fun session. Foreigners had a field day," one trader said.
Telecommunications firm Telmex and retail stock Cifra led the rally, traders said. Telmex L shares and Cifra B and C shares accounted for one-quarter of all shares traded.
Telmex L shares ended up 24 centavos at 15.72 pesos, and Cifra B shares gained 28 centavos to 12.20 pesos.
Telmex ADRs also fended off a slide in the Dow Jones to end up 3/4 at 40-3/4, a level unseen since the December 1994 peso crisis.
Dealers said Cifra gained on news it will propose a dividend to its shareholders and on stock upgrades from international brokerages.
On the broad market, 128 stocks changed hands, of which gainers .PG.MX trounced decliners .PL.MX by 71 to 26.
Cellphone company Iusacell topped the decliners, off 84 centavos at 8.50 pesos.
Traders said dealers sold Iusacel stock after the company reported a net loss for 1996 during the session.
Technical analysts noted the IPC receded from an intraday record of 3,912.66 points set in early trade.

"The IPC is overbought and several indicators are looking tired. After today's rally, a rest would be good for the market to gather steam before gaining once more," said Jaime Fernandez, an analyst with the Interacciones brokerage.
"Nonetheless, I think it should return to 3,750 points to take a run at the 4,000-point mark. It's not the bullet that kills you, but how fast it's shot," he added.
